key_insight: Disagreement between fixed numerical rewards and expert preferences can reveal promising materials that automated scores overlook.
engineering_relevance: Expert-guided generative models could broaden materials screening beyond rigid metrics, including electronic flatness, synthesizability, and phonon properties.
method: Compare expert judgments of electronic flat bands with a numerical bandwidth score.
Learn expert preferences from pairwise comparisons.
Use learned preferences to guide a crystal diffusion model.
evidence_signal: Systematic expert–score disagreements exceeded what an estimated 5% mistaken-label rate could explain; learned preferences favored reported partially flat-band compounds KCo2As2 and CoGa that the score would discard.
watch_item: Preference-guided candidates still require independent validation; expert alignment alone does not establish synthesizability or useful material performance.
paper_title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
